sections.content: Spanish commonly uses se impersonal and *hay* *que* to describe how something works without focusing on a particular person. Se + third-person singular is useful for general procedures: Se *introduce* la *tarjeta*. Hay que *seguir* las *instrucciones*.

items.spanish: Se introduce la tarjeta en la máquina.
items.english: The card is inserted into the machine.

items.spanish: Se pulsa este botón para empezar.
items.english: This button is pressed to start.
You have to follow the instructions.

items.spanish: Para usar el sistema, se necesita una contraseña.
items.english: To use the system, a password is needed.

sections.content: Use se impersonal when the person performing the action is not important or is deliberately left general.
